text:
Jess: Hey — running into a weird TS typing failure when consumers import our JS SDK from an edge environment (ESM). Typescript errors show up only for generic overloads and when `tsconfig` has `module: 'ESNext'`
Mike: Can you paste the error?
Jess: Sure — this happens at call site when using `client.generate<T>(...)` — TS2345-ish: 
```
error TS2345: Argument of type '...' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Prompt<T>'.
```
The type inference collapses to `any` or fails to match overloads that exist in `dist/index.d.ts`.
Tara: Do you emit `declaration` files and `types` in package.json? ESM + CJS dual packages often mispoint `types` to a CJS build and tooling resolves the wrong entry.
Jess: We do `declaration: true` but our package.json `exports` block points only to `./dist/index.mjs` for `import` and `./dist/index.cjs` for `require`. `types` points to `dist/index.d.ts`.
Sam: Can you share tsconfig? My hunch: `moduleResolution` and `target` affect generic inference across ESM boundaries, and `skipLibCheck` can hide mismatch. Also `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` may change how the .d.ts shapes are interpreted.
Jess: tsconfig: 
```
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "node",
    "declaration": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": false,
    "strict": true
  }
}
```
Sam: Try toggling `moduleResolution` to `node16`/`bundler` if you're using ESM exports with conditional exports. Node16 resolution follows exports/conditional logic more closely which affects how TS finds the .d.ts for `import`.
Mike: Another common pitfall: overloads + generics can be fragile across .d.ts boundaries. If your `generate` API has multiple overloads like `generate<T>(opts: A<T>)` and `generate(opts: B)`, TS sometimes can't pick the right overload without an explicit generic param. Suggest collapsing to a single generic with discriminated unions or provide documented explicit generic usage `client.generate<MyResp>(...)` as a workaround.
Tara: Also check if you accidentally emit `export =` style types in d.ts when consumers expect ESM `export default` — that will make inference weird. `declaration` + `esModuleInterop` sometimes generate mismatches.
Jess: Repro: in a Next.js Edge function (Vercel Edge runtime) importing our ESM bundle gives: 
```
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.KEY });
const resp = await client.generate({ prompt: 'x' }); // -> type error at compile
```
But when same package consumed in Node (CJS) it types OK.
Sam: That strongly hints the resolver picks a different .d.ts (or none) in the Edge build pipeline. Vercel/next uses `module: "esnext"` and swc to strip types; but the bundler needs correct `exports` and `types` fields. Double-check top-level `types` and `exports."./package".types` mappings if present.
Mike: Quick checks: 
- Ensure `package.json` has `types` pointing to the ESM d.ts entry (e.g., `dist/index.d.ts`).
- Add "typesVersions" mapping if you need different types for `import` vs `require`.
- Consider emitting a tiny `./dist/esm.d.ts` that mirrors the ESM surface without conditional overload shims.

Tara: For the `unknown` vs `any` part: if your API accepts `unknown` payloads internally but your generic expects `T = any`, inference can widen to `unknown` causing users to add `as any`. Recommend using `T = unknown` only at internal boundaries and expose `T = any` for DX, or better still use `T extends object = Record<string, any>` to keep inference workable.
Jess: Good point — some users complained they had to write `generate<Record<string, string>>` explicitly.
Sam: Workaround patches we can try quickly: 
1) Add a small ESM-specific `index.d.mts`/`index.d.ts` (explicit exports) so resolution is unambiguous.
2) Run `tsc --traceResolution` in a minimal repro to see which .d.ts file TS picks.
3) For overloads, add a single fallthrough signature with a generic: `generate<T = unknown>(opts: GenerateOptions<T>): Promise<GenerateResult<T>>` after overloads — that helps inference.
Mike: Action: I'll add a minimal repro in `sdk/samples/edge-typing` and a GH Action that runs `tsc` in both `module:ESNext` and `module:CommonJS` modes. Assigning to me. @Tara can you review the proposed d.ts changes?
Tara: Yep. I'll also test on Next + SWC and Vercel Edge to ensure bundler resolution picks the right types.
ryan-ci-bot: CI: build (edge-typing-repro) failed on 1 test — `tsc` emitted errors in sample project.
Jess: Thanks — I'll paste the failing trace soon. For the commit message when we fix it: `devex: fix ESM edge typing + overload inference` :thumbsup:
Mike: Sounds good. If we end up needing a breaking doc change, we should add a short note to the quickstart about explicit generic usage in edge runtimes.
Jess: Agreed — less friction for users.
Sam: TL;DR: likely resolver picks wrong .d.ts for ESM; workaround by stronger single-generic signature + explicit ESM d.ts entry; we'll add repro and tests.
